subtitle: A Composer's Field Guide
author: Jonathan Romanovský
back_blurb: How can a composer make time, attention, and feeling vivid while using limited musical means? This compact field guide approaches ambient and minimalist music through acts: attending, limiting, sustaining, repeating, drifting, layering, coloring, releasing control, placing, and discovering form. It moves between composers including Cage, Eno, Feldman, Eastman, Brahms, and Oliveros, then returns each idea to choices a musician can make. It offers no recipe for serenity. Repetition may comfort or threaten; a drone may shelter or exert pressure. The aim is practical: to help composers make fewer choices more consequential.
author_bio: Jonathan Romanovský is a generated authorial persona: a consistent working voice combining the perspectives of a music theorist, practicing composer, improviser, and teacher. The book was developed through an extended collaboration between Alesh Houdek and an AI language model. Houdek conceived and directed the project, shaped its structure and examples, guided revisions, and wrote the Foreword.
